response.answer: For adherence metrics and clinical outcomes, use multiple imputation and consider Missing Not At Random (MNAR) models for sensitivity analyses.

results.title: Analytical approaches and estimands to take account of ...
results.content: The handling of missing data plays a key role in defining estimands.Citation7,Citation9,Citation13,Citation15–Citation17 The ICH-E9-R1 addendum on estimands and sensitivity analyses states that estimands are defined by the target population; the outcome of interest; the specification of how post-randomization events (eg, dropout, treatment withdrawal, noncompliance, rescue medication) are reflected in the research question; and the summary measure (such as difference in means or odds ratio) for the endpoint.Citation18 Estimands can be classified into two categories based on adherence to the protocol.Citation17 Efficacy, sometimes called de jure (by the rules, per protocol), is the effect of the intervention under full compliance with the treatment protocol. Knowing which variables are associated with missingness can also be helpful for modeling, as they can be included in multiple imputation (MI) models and the weight model for inverse probability-weighted generalized estimating equations (GEEs).Citation26 Missing primary outcome data rates at each time point, by intervention arm, should be shown in the CONSORT participant flow diagram.Citation27.
